body.statement: Using \(\mathsf H_{\rm prof}\), determine the explicit piecewise function \(r_{n,K}(a,\beta)\) and the maximal \(\kappa_{\max}\) such that \(\rho^\star_{n,K}(a,\epsilon_{\rm tot})\asymp r_{n,K}(a,\beta)\) uniformly whenever \(K\le n^{\kappa_{\max}}\). Derive the exact transition surfaces obtained by balancing \(r_{\rm dense}\), \(r_{\rm tail}\), \(r_{\rm train}\), and the least-favorable active-face scale \(r_{\rm face}\). The formula must agree with the fixed-\(K\) upper bound and, if the legal dense construction is established, must not fall below \(r_{\rm dense}\) in that construction's regime.
body.justification: The piecewise radius is the paper's named theorem-level focal object.
body.gap: Breunig and Chen characterize structural-space NPIV testing, and Marteau and Sapatinas characterize a diagonal Gaussian sequence experiment; neither result determines this observed-image radius.
body.consumer: The frontier converts support size and proxy strength into a checkable detectability limit for discrete one-NCO diagnostics.

obligation.what_is_open: The exact piecewise minimax radius, active-face scale, transition surfaces, and maximal polynomial dimension exponent remain undetermined.
obligation.obstruction: The proved dense converse and finite-sample projection upper bound have different exponents, while the missing profiled operator converse prevents deciding whether either training term is intrinsic. Arbitrary legal output rotations also rule out an unproved output-frequency truncation argument.
obligation.attempted: The fixed-support scalar path, a positive DCT dense block, and the fully uniform projection comparison were derived. Balancing only those certified terms gives a bracket and a sufficient dimension range, but does not identify the minimax frontier.
obligation.partial_result:
The finite-sample theorem and the scalar converse yield the honest bracket
\[
 c n^{-1/2}
 \ \le\ \rho^\star_{n,K}(a,\epsilon_{\rm tot})
 \ \le\ C\left\{\sqrt{K/n}+R\sqrt{KS_\beta(K)/n}+\sqrt{K\log K/n}\right\},
\]
under the regular-subclass premise of \(\mathrm{thm:fixed\mbox{-}k\mbox{-}transverse\mbox{-}lower}\).  In the dense regime \(K=o(n^{2/3})\) and \(K^{-(a+\beta)}\lesssim K^{1/4}/\sqrt n\), the left side strengthens to \(c\max\{n^{-1/2},K^{1/4}/\sqrt n\}\) under the explicit link-slack compatibility condition in \(\mathrm{thm:legal\mbox{-}dense\mbox{-}block\mbox{-}partial}\).  The displayed upper bound shrinks for polynomial \(K=n^\kappa\) whenever \(\kappa<1\) if \(\beta\ge1/2\), and whenever \(\kappa<\{2(1-\beta)\}^{-1}\) if \(0<\beta<1/2\).  These are certified sufficient growth ranges for the conservative test, not the unknown maximal minimax range.
